newsitem.title: INDIA: Ousted Indian PM blames old politicians.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Indian PM blames old politicians.

text.p: Former Indian prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda, striking a reflective note on his first full day out of office, on Tuesday criticised ageing politicians and said people had lost faith in their leaders.

Speaking a day after he handed over the post he held for 10 months to Inder Kumar Gujral, Deve Gowda told a business conference: "We old politicians, we are a little bit accustomed to manipulative politics and manoeuvring."
Deve Gowda's government was defeated in a confidence vote on April 11, provoked by the Congress party's decision to withdraw its support for the administration.

Congress president Sitaram Kesri, 77, later said the party was willing to support a new centre-left coalition, but only if Deve Gowda was replaced as its leader. Deve Gowda's alliance initially resisted Kesri's demand but finally gave in.

"The people have lost faith in their leaders. Power is the main motto of politics, to achieve power we will do everything, moral or immoral. It is the beginning of the saddest event in Indian politics," said Deve Gowda, speaking softly and slowly.
"Only the younger generation...will save this country from the hands of the traditional politicians who are known for their manipulations and manoeuvring," he said.
The defeated prime minister said India had been on the verge of taking off when he was toppled. "Then, all of a sudden, some political developments took place," Deve Gowda said.
"But I have still (got) confidence. I am optimistic," he added. "There is no need to cry over spilt milk."
